Hi Asha — quick follow up on the rotation and handoff details:

On-call & TAM model (summary):
- Named TAM (your primary point of contact) during 9am–6pm PT, M–F; TAM covers proactive reviews, weekly syncs, and runbook updates.
- 24x7 engineering on-call rotation (3-week primary rotation per region) for P1s. Typical pages: PagerDuty with escalation from on-call engineer -> on-call engineering lead -> on-call principal engineer -> on-call product on-call -> support director.
- Regional coverage: US/EU/APAC overlaps for shift handovers; for regulated customers we can provide business-hours TAMs in your preferred region.

Incident comms templates (excerpt):
- Initial alert (within 15 min): short summary, impact scope, mitigation in progress, expected next update window.
- Status update cadence: every 30 minutes until mitigation progress; hourly updates once stabilized for P1s.
- Post-incident: private postmortem within 5 business days for P1; public-facing summary within 7 business days if customer agrees.

On runbook access: we provide read-only links to customer-specific runbooks that include playbooks for common failure modes. Full internal runbooks are redacted; we can schedule a controlled walkthrough with your security team if needed.

If you want a version of the spreadsheet that maps each question in your appendix to our answer, we can produce that by EOB Monday.

Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

2) Runbook access: will the read-only links be accessible from our corporate network only, or can we consume them externally? Our security team prefers SSO access and conditional access policies.
3) For the on-call escalation chain: can you confirm the guaranteed engineer escalation time to a principal engineer for P1s after the initial page? We need this for our executive runbook.

If you can put those three items in the consolidated spreadsheet and include a sample incident timeline (with timestamps), that will speed procurement review.

Thanks — Asha
